catalog_quote: [1998/2011, p. 14] A szó főhangsúlya általában az első szótagra esik: wŏntəŋ ‘erdei’, imi ‘anyó'. Háromnál többtagú szavakban a harmadik szótagon mellékhangsúly van: ḳåtɣəʌamən ‘a mi kettőnk két háza'. Azokban az esetekben, amikor az első szótagban [-tense], a második szótagban [+tense] magánhangzó van, a hangsúly áttolódik a második szótagra: səran ‘zürjén’, səɣʌam ‘menyhalaim’, ḳŏrnat ‘képpel'. A mondat ereszkedő hanglejtésű. A közlés céljának megfelelően a kiemelendő szavak hangsúlyos szótagai a többinél magasabb hangfekvésűek. Kérdő mondatban a kérdezett szó intonációja szintén meredeken eső: mənʌən? ‘Elmész?’ || [2017, pp. 58-59] Главное ударение в основном падает на первый слог: вӧнтəӈ ‘лесной’, ими ‘женщина’. Последующие нечетные слоги несут на себе второстепенное ударение: ӄотҳəԓамəн ‘два дома нас двоих’. Ударение не имеет фонематического значения, то есть оно не выполняет смыслоразличительной роли. В русских заимствованиях ударение ставится либо на первый слог, либо на тот слог, на котором оно стоит в русском языке. В потоке речи смысловые, экспрессивные и другие факторы могут внести изменение во фразовое и словесное ударение.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: A szó főhangsúlya általában az első szótagra esik: wŏntəŋ 'erdei', imi 'anyó'. Háromnál többtagú szavakban a harmadik szótagon mellékhangsúly van: ḳåtɣəʌamən 'a mi kettőnk két háza'. new_statements.translation: The main stress of the word generally falls on the first syllable: wŏntəŋ 'of the forest', imi 'old woman'. In words of more than three syllables there is a secondary stress on the third syllable: ḳåtɣəʌamən 'the two houses of the two of us'. In those cases where the first syllable contains a [-tense] vowel and the second syllable a [+tense] vowel, the stress shifts to the second syllable: səran 'Zyrian (Komi)', səɣʌam 'my burbots', ḳŏrnat 'with a picture'.
new_statements.citation: Csepregi, Márta. 1998/2011. Szurguti osztják chrestomathia (Studia uralo-altaica supplementum 6). Szeged: JATE Finnugor Tanszék; 2011 revised edition (rev. Csepregi Márta, Gugán Katalin, Kováts Zsófia), PDF distributed by the LMU Ob-Ugric database.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default main stress on the first syllable; when the first-syllable vowel is reduced ([-tense], schwa-type) and the second-syllable vowel is full ([+tense]), main stress moves to the second syllable. Full vs. reduced vowel quantity is the conditioning factor, so the pattern is quantity-sensitive with an initial default (the same author's 2017 Russian edition, p. 58, gives only 'main stress mostly on the first syllable' and omits the shift rule, which would read as fixed: initial syllable).
new_statements.secondary_stress: 1998/2011 p. 14: secondary stress on the third syllable in words of more than three syllables (ḳåtɣəʌamən). 2017 p. 58: 'Последующие нечетные слоги несут на себе второстепенное ударение' (following odd-numbered syllables carry secondary stress).
new_statements.exceptions: Reduced V1 + full V2 words take second-syllable stress (səran, səɣʌam, ḳŏrnat). 2017 ed. p. 58 adds: stress is not phonemic ('не имеет фонематического значения'); Russian loans are stressed either on the first syllable or where Russian stresses them; p. 59: in connected speech semantic/expressive factors can change phrasal and word stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress ('a szó főhangsúlya'), cited forms are isolated words; sentence intonation treated separately (falling; stressed syllables of emphasised words pitched higher; steep fall on the questioned word). Reading confidence is medium because the two editions by the same author differ on whether the second-syllable shift exists.
new_statements.identity_note: Csepregi's chrestomathy describes Surgut Khanty proper (surg1248; the 2017 edition names the Lyamin, Pim, Tromagan, Agan, Little/Big Yugan, Salym and Demyanka varieties, with A. S. Pesikova as native consultant/editor). Filchenko 2007, which Glottolog's bibliography files under surg1248 and Grambank codes surg1248 from, actually describes the Vasyugan and Alexandrovo dialects of Eastern Khanty (Glottolog: Vasjugan Khanty vasj1234, a dialect of Vach-Vasjugan fare1244), not Surgut; its stress description (initial default, second-syllable stress with reduced V1 + full V2, multiple stresses) nevertheless parallels Csepregi's.

tone_statements.citation: Рыжикова, Татьяна Раисовна. 2022. Интонационное оформление побудительных высказываний (на материале обско-угорских и тюркских языков Сибири) [Intonation of imperative utterances (Ob-Ugric and Turkic languages of Siberia)]. Вестник угроведения 12(3): 514–525.
tone_statements.quote: Интонационно приказ оформляется нисходящим движением тона с пиком интенсивности на первом слоге (рис. 10). … Таким образом, по нашим экспериментальным данным повелительная интонация в сургутском диалекте маркируется деклинацией, если есть дополнительные члены предложения, тон – восходяще-нисходящий. Поскольку отрицательная форма – прохибитив – образуется при помощи специальной частицы, именно она маркируется восходяще-нисходящим тоном вне зависимости от позиции сказуемого в высказывании.
tone_statements.translation: Intonationally a command is shaped by a falling pitch movement with the intensity peak on the first syllable (fig. 10). … Thus, on our experimental data, imperative intonation in the Surgut dialect is marked by declination; if there are additional sentence constituents, the pitch contour is rising-falling. Since the negative form, the prohibitive, is formed with a special particle, it is this particle that carries the rising-falling contour regardless of the position of the predicate in the utterance.

sources.quote: Die Betonung im Ostjakischen ist dynamisch. In zwei- oder mehrsilbigen Wörtern liegt sie gewöhnlich auf der ersten Silbe. Infolge der Qualität der Vokale bzw. Offenheit oder Geschlossenheit der Silbe kann die Betonung auf die zweite Silbe verlagert werden. Die Betonung hat keine bedeutungsdifferenzierende Funktion.

sources.note: Sec. 1.7 'Stress', pp. 57-60: 'Stress in Eastern Khanty is dynamic. In bi- or poly-syllabic words, the stress is often assigned to the word-initial syllable'; second-syllable stress when syllable 1 has a reduced vowel (or is closed) and syllable 2 a full vowel; polysyllables carry multiple stresses (1st+3rd or 2nd+4th); trisyllables fluctuate; stress not phonologically relevant (no minimal pairs). Vasyugan/Alexandrovo, not Surgut proper.

sources.note: Praat-aided discourse-prosody pilot on Surgut Khanty intonation units: 'tone' here means the IU pitch contour (sharp rise, slow fall, pitch reset after pause; interrogatives end near starting pitch). Lexical tone never mentioned in the 18 pp; first-syllable word accent credited to Csepregi 1998.

tone.quote: Generally, the tone of a IU in Khanty starts with a radical rise to a peak and begins falling more slowly than it rose. The highlight of the tone is usually the first syllable of the main word of the first NP, usually the subject NP. ... As the pitch falls to the IU boundary, the pitch may slightly rise several times. The peaks of these small rises are usually the main accents in the words. The ending tone is generally lower than the starting one. After a pause, the pitch is reset at the new IU.

sources.citation: Уртегешев, Николай Сергеевич & Наталья Борисовна Кошкарёва. 2018. Инвентарь прерывистых гласных фонем в сургутском диалекте хантыйского языка [An inventory of intermittent vowel phonemes in the Surgut dialect of Khanty]. Сибирский филологический журнал 2018(1): 180–207.
sources.note: Not about pitch: posits a class of 'interrupted' (прерывистые) long first-syllable vowel phonemes, i.e. vowel nuclei broken by a glottal closure and produced with strong pharyngeal tension (optionally labialised/nasalised), forming a single syllable; four such phonemes identified by distribution, plus 'incompletely formed' interrupted vowels intermediate to diphthongoids. A laryngealisation/glottalisation claim at the level of the vowel system, relevant to word-prosodic typology (stød-like nuclei) but given a purely segmental analysis; no tonal interpretation offered.
